questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code uses its worker pool to deliver a campaign? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The pool is built with `poolSize` core and max threads and a `LinkedBlockingQueue<>()` with no capacity. A marketing tool submits 50,000 campaigns in a burst while every worker is busy. What happens?
choices: Submissions beyond poolSize are rejected with RejectedExecutionException
The pool grows beyond poolSize threads to absorb the burst
The calling thread runs the excess campaigns itself, slowing the caller
All campaigns are accepted into the queue, so memory use grows with the backlog while thread count stays at poolSize

questions.prompt: One call to `gateway.push` throws an IOException for a single device token while the rest of the campaign is healthy. What is the effect?
choices: That token is counted in `failed`; the other tokens are still processed and the worker thread survives
The whole campaign future fails with the IOException and no audit record is written
The worker thread that ran the push dies and the pool shrinks by one
The remaining tokens in the campaign are skipped

questions.prompt: `result.get(5, SECONDS)` throws TimeoutException for a slow push. What is true afterwards?
choices: The push task is cancelled automatically when the timeout elapses
The push may still run or complete later even though it was already counted as failed
The worker thread running the push is interrupted and replaced
The timeout is retried once with a doubled wait
